music.heading: NeuralDeep music generation
music.intro: POST /v1/audio/speech with model=llmgateway/music uses Google Lyria 3 Pro. The gateway creates a task, polls every 3 seconds and returns the completed audio file. The wait is limited to 360 seconds (HTTP 504); failed generation returns HTTP 502. Once a task ID is received, it is never submitted again. If a backup route is configured, these errors trigger switching to it.
music.input: Required nonempty string describing genre, instruments, mood and vocals. Sent to NeuralDeep as prompt.
music.lyrics: Lyrics with [verse], [chorus] and [bridge] tags. Use [instrumental] for instrumental music.
music.vocal_language: Vocal language, for example ru or en.
music.audio_duration: Desired duration from 10 to 300 seconds. Exact duration is not guaranteed.
music.bpm: Desired tempo in beats per minute.
music.response_format: mp3 (default), wav, wav32, flac, opus or aac. Sent as audio_format when downloading the track.
music.limits: Fields other than model and input are optional. bpm, key_scale and time_signature are model hints; the official reference does not specify exact types or ranges. voice, speed and instructions do not control music; the voice catalog is empty and stream=true is unsupported. NeuralDeep discards unknown fields; covers, fragment editing, separate stems, files and other task_type values are unavailable.
music.playground: In Playground, open Text to Speech, select llmgateway/music, enter the music description, choose a format, disable Dialogue and click Generate speech. Leave Voice and Instructions empty. A player and download link appear when the track is ready. The form currently has no lyrics, vocal_language, audio_duration, bpm, key_scale, time_signature, seed or batch_size fields; send those through the API, as shown below.
music.fallback: For music routes starting with NeuralDeep /music/generate, subsequent entries are tried on quota exhaustion (HTTP 429), provider 5xx errors, network errors or timeouts. llmgateway/music is configured as NeuralDeep → sa3/sa3-medium. Request errors 400/401/402/422 do not trigger switching. For sa3-medium, audio_duration is sent as seconds; the default is 30 seconds when no duration is supplied. The backup request contains only model, input, seconds and response_format: lyrics and other NeuralDeep-specific parameters are not forwarded. Attempts appear in the fallback log; a successful call is billed once against the provider that returned the audio.
music.cooldown: When NeuralDeep returns 429 with a reset time in Retry-After, X-Quota-Reset or error.reset_at, the gateway stores a cooldown, a temporary pause for that model and key. New requests skip NeuralDeep and use the next route until that time; afterwards NeuralDeep is tried again. The latest valid reset time wins when several are supplied. No cooldown is assigned without a valid future reset time. State is kept in process memory and is cleared on restart.

sfx.heading: SFX: sound effect prompt rules
sfx.intro: Use POST /v1/audio/speech with model=llmgateway/small-sfx. Describe the audible result in input using ordinary Russian or English. Russian descriptions are automatically translated and refined; special tags and model commands are unnecessary.
sfx.audible: Describe the source, action, sound character, distance, surroundings and development over time. Appearance and plot matter only when they affect the sound.
sfx.kinds: Distinguish a single effect, continuous ambience and a scene with events. The service chooses how to prepare the sound; for a scene, it prepares sources separately and places them on the timeline.
sfx.duration: State the total duration explicitly, preferably as a whole number of seconds, up to 120. If omitted, the service chooses it: typical guidelines are 2–6 seconds for an effect, 10–20 for ambience and 15–40 for a sequence. An event timestamp does not specify total recording length.
sfx.fraction: Fractional duration is rounded up: 1.2 seconds produces a 2-second recording with a gradual fade after 1.2 seconds. The separate duration parameter takes precedence over duration in input; keep them consistent.
sfx.timeline: For complex scenes, specify each source’s start and end, continuous background, pauses, event counts and volume changes. Give separate timestamps for three impacts; describe differences if they should sound different.
sfx.acoustics: Replace “epic” or “high quality” with audible properties: a dull low impact, a thin chime with a long decay, a dry close click without echo. Start with the main sound, avoid contradictions and leave time for pauses and decay.
sfx.quality: Request effects separately for independent control. A timeline does not guarantee subsecond onset accuracy within generated fragments. Listen to check character, impact count, unwanted noise and seamless looping. Automatic quality checks and regeneration are not currently available.
sfx.example: Total duration 18 seconds. Quiet wind rustles the leaves throughout. Birdsong is audible from the beginning until second 6. At second 6, one distant gunshot sounds; the birds fall silent at that moment. From second 10, the birds return and sing slightly louder until the end. The wind continues without interruption. No speech or music.
sfx.guide: Full agent instructions: all 7 rules, examples and a universal template. Open or download the Markdown file to pass it to an agent.

jinaSearch.summary: Equivalent to s.jina.ai: GET with a q query parameter or a query in the path /v1/jina/search/your%20query. POST with JSON or form data is also supported. Reads the full result pages; authenticate with a gateway Bearer key.
jinaSearch.q: Search query in the q field.
jinaSearch.model: Search model from web_search and reader model from web_read. Each field is optional when its section contains exactly one configured model.
jinaSearch.count: Number of results: num or count, from 1 to 20, default 10; num takes precedence.
jinaSearch.site: Restrict domains with a string or an array of strings; form requests can repeat site. hl sets the search language, default en.
jinaSearch.format: X-Respond-With or respondWith: markdown (default) or text. The header takes precedence.
jinaSearch.response: Accept: application/json returns JSON with code (200), status (20000) and a data array. Each item contains title, url, description and the full page content. Otherwise returns text with numbered Title, URL Source, Description and page contents.
jinaSearch.limits: Access is checked for both models. Charged as one web_search operation. Search or page-reading failures fail the whole request with a gateway-format error. GET and POST support the same parameters; no-content and streaming are not implemented.

jina.summary: Jina Reader: GET with a url query parameter or a page URL in the path /v1/jina/extract/https://example.com. POST with JSON or form data is also supported. Authenticate with a gateway Bearer key.
jina.model: A model from web_read. Optional when exactly one model is configured; specify model explicitly when multiple models are configured.
jina.respondWith: Content format: markdown (default) or text. Set the respondWith field or the X-Respond-With header; the header takes precedence.
jina.accept: Accept: application/json returns JSON with code (200), status (20000) and data. The data object contains title, description, url and content. Otherwise returns text with Title, URL Source and Markdown Content; text format returns only the page content.
jina.limits: For GET with a page URL in the path, the query string remains part of the page URL. Use GET with a url query parameter for model and respondWith options. CSS selectors, screenshots and browser controls are not supported. Errors use the gateway format; charged as web_read.
